title: Attach a finite family of nondegenerate simplices to a split truncation
statement: Let $\mathcal D$ be a category with finite limits [def-galois-finite-limits-colimits], and let $n\geq0$. Let $K:\Delta_{\leq n}^{op}\to\mathrm{SR}(\mathcal D)$ be an $n$-truncated simplicial object [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-coskeleton, def-weil-pbc-formal-coproduct], with $K_q=\{U_{q,i}\}_{i\in I_q}$ and all $I_q$ finite. Assume $K$ is split in the following explicit sense: writing $N_q\subseteq I_q$ for indices not in the image of any operator associated to a surjection $[q]\to[r]$ with $r<q$, the map $\coprod_{0\leq r\leq q,\,\sigma:[q]\twoheadrightarrow[r]}N_r\to I_q$, $(\sigma,i)\mapsto K(\sigma)(i)$, is bijective, and the corresponding component morphisms $U_{r,i}\to U_{q,K(\sigma)(i)}$ are isomorphisms. Let $M$ be the limit in $\mathrm{SR}(\mathcal D)$ of the boundary diagram with objects $K_n^{(a)}$ ($0\leq a\leq n+1$), objects $K_{n-1}^{(a,b)}$ ($a<b$) and arrows $d_{b-1}:K_n^{(a)}\to K_{n-1}^{(a,b)}$, $d_a:K_n^{(b)}\to K_{n-1}^{(a,b)}$ (for $n=0$, just two copies of $K_0$ and no arrows). For any finite family $V=\{V_j\}_{j\in J}$ with a morphism $v:V\to M$, there is a split $(n+1)$-truncated simplicial object $L$ extending $K$, with $L_{n+1}=V\amalg\coprod_{0\leq r\leq n,\,\sigma:[n+1]\twoheadrightarrow[r]}\{U_{r,i}\}_{i\in N_r}$. Its new nondegenerate indices are precisely $J$, its boundary morphism $L_{n+1}\to M$ restricts to $v$ on $V$, and on the summand $(\sigma,i)$ its $a$-th face is the component of $K(\sigma\circ\delta_a)$ on $U_{r,i}$, where $\delta_a:[n]\hookrightarrow[n+1]$ omits $a$. Every term of $L$ has finite index set.

source.place: Tag 0DAV, lemma-hypercovering-object, proof: construction of the extension and its simplicial operators; Tag 0DAU, lemma-split, for the explicit split convention. This is the categorical attachment part, before imposing covering conditions.

proof.text: Put h=n+1 and P_r={U_{r,i}}_{i∈N_r} for r≤n, P_h=V. For q≤n let H_q be the formal family of triples (r,σ,i), with σ:[q]↠[r] and i∈N_r. The split hypothesis gives a componentwise isomorphism E_q:H_q→K_q, whose component e_{σ,i} is K(σ)|_{U_{r,i}}. Set H_h to the displayed new family, also regarding V_j as the triple (h,id,j). Eventually transport the operators on H_q through E_q for q≤n, so the resulting L agrees exactly with K in those degrees. Each H_q has finite index set: N_r is a subset of finite I_r, and there are finitely many functions between any two finite ordinals.

proof.text: For every α:[q]→[h] with q≤n define B_α:V→K_q as follows. Choose a missing value a of α and write α=δ_aβ; put B_α=K(β)v_a. For two missing values a<b, α factors through the injection κ omitting both a and b, say α=κγ. Writing κ=δ_aδ_{b-1}=δ_bδ_a gives K(β)v_a=K(γ) d_{b-1}v_a and K(β′)v_b=K(γ) d_a v_b. These agree by the defining equality of the limit M. For n=0 no map α:[q]→[1] with q≤0 can omit both values, so there is no independence condition. Moreover B_{αβ}=K(β)B_α whenever q,p≤n and β:[p]→[q], using the same missing value a. For a proper injection τ:[t]↪[h] write b_τ=B_τ; for an injection τ:[t]↪[r] with r≤n, write b_τ=K(τ)|_{P_r}. These are morphisms of formal families, including their index functions, and they obey b_{τη}=K(η)b_τ for injections η into [t]. Set b_id=id on P_r, including P_h.

proof.text: Define F(α):H_b→H_a for EVERY order-preserving α:[a]→[b], a,b≤h. On a source summand (r,σ,i), factor σ α=τ ρ uniquely, where ρ:[a]↠[t] enumerates the image and τ:[t]↪[r] is its increasing inclusion. If t=h then a=b=r=h and σ=α=τ=ρ=id, so use the identity on V_i. Otherwise apply the component of b_τ to P_{r,i}, obtaining an index k of K_t and a map f:P_{r,i}→U_{t,k}. The split bijection writes k uniquely as K(λ)(j), λ:[t]↠[u], j∈N_u. Send this component to the summand (u,λρ,j) of H_a by e_{λ,j}^{-1}f. This includes maps into the new degree even when α is not surjective, and all nonidentity endomorphisms of [h]. For a,b≤n it is exactly E_a^{-1}K(α)E_b, because K(ρ)K(τ) applied to the source component is K(σα), and K(ρ)e_{λ,j}=e_{λρ,j}. The last equality also proves that a surjection α simply sends (r,σ,i) to (r,σα,i) with identity component.

proof.text: Check composition for α:[a]→[b] and β:[p]→[a] componentwise. In the notation of step 3, let k=K(λ)(j) be the index of b_τ(i). Factor ρβ=ηγ, with η:[s]↪[t], γ:[p]↠[s]. Then σαβ=(τη)γ is the image factorization for the composite, and b_{τη}(i)=K(η)b_τ(i) by step 2 (or functoriality of K when r≤n). The second operator, applied to the intermediate summand (u,λρ,j), factors λρβ: factor λη=ξζ, with ξ injective and ζ surjective, so its image factorization is ξ(ζγ). Since t,u,s≤n, functoriality in the old truncation gives K(η)e_{λ,j}=K(λη)|_{P_{u,j}}=K(ζ)K(ξ)|_{P_{u,j}}. If K(ξ)(j)=K(μ)(l), split normalization therefore makes the final label (w,μζγ,l) and final component e_{μ,l}^{-1}(K(ξ)|_{P_{u,j}}) e_{λ,j}^{-1}f on the two-step route. On the direct route K(η)f=K(ζ)(K(ξ)|_{P_{u,j}})e_{λ,j}^{-1}f; its normalization uses label μζ in degree s and e_{μζ,l}=K(ζ)e_{μ,l}, giving exactly the same final label and component. All these e-maps are the component isomorphisms supplied by the split hypothesis. The exceptional t=h case is an identity operator, and if the direct composite has image h then both factors are identities on [h]. Thus F(β)F(α)=F(αβ) in every case; the identity formula follows by normalizing σ itself. Transport F through E_q in degrees q≤n and the identity in degree h to obtain the required functor L. Surjections into degree h send the old normalized labels to (r,σα,i), with identity components, so their images are exactly all summands with r≤n and none in J. Every such summand is obtained using σ itself. Hence the new nondegenerate set is J and the split component maps are identities. Step 2 gives the prescribed faces on V, while step 3 in a lower target gives K(σδ_a) on each old degenerate summand. Finiteness follows from step 1. When n=0, L_1=V⨿K_0. When n=1, the three surjections give the families P_0 and two copies of P_1, so L_2=V⨿P_0⨿P_1⨿P_1; the actual number of old summands is |N_0|+2|N_1|, not necessarily three. Empty families, empty objects, and J=∅ require no change to any formula.
